instructions: Put the 4 eggs in a saucepan and cover them with cold water by about an inch. Bring it to a full boil over high heat, then cover the pan, take it off the heat and leave it for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Whisk 2/3 cup mayonnaise, 1/4 cup sour cream, 1 1/2 tsp dried parsley, 1/2 tsp dried dill, 1/4 tsp onion powder, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper in a small bowl.
Whisk in the 3 tbsp milk a spoonful at a time, until the dressing pours. Put it in the fridge.

Lay 8 slices of bacon in a large cold skillet and turn the heat to medium. Cook them, turning now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until they're crisp and deep golden. Move them to a plate lined with paper towel.
Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the bacon fat and keep the pan for the chicken.
When the eggs have had their 15 minutes, lift them into a bowl of ice water and leave them for 5 minutes.
Cut each chicken breast in half through the side so you have thin cutlets. Pat them dry and sprinkle both sides with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper and the 1/2 tsp paprika.
Heat the bacon fat over medium high until it shimmers. Add the cutlets and leave them alone for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and they let go of the pan.

Flip them and cook the other side for about 3 minutes. You're cooking them to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest one. No thermometer? Cut into it: it's done when there's no pink left.
Move the chicken to a board and let it rest for 5 minutes, then slice it into strips.
While it rests, cut the romaine into bite size pieces, wash it and dry it well. Halve 1 cup of the cherry tomatoes and thinly slice half the red onion.
Peel the eggs and cut them into quarters. Break the bacon into pieces.
Halve the avocado, take out the pit and slice it. Do this last. Cut avocado turns brown if it sits.
Spread the romaine over a large platter or four plates. Lay the chicken, eggs, avocado, tomatoes, onion and bacon over it in rows, then scatter the blue cheese across the top.
Serve with the dressing on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions top chopped romaine with chicken, bacon, hard boiled eggs, avocado, tomato and blue cheese. Spend With Pennies dresses it with a creamy herb dressing of mayonnaise, sour cream, dried parsley and dill thinned with milk, and cooks thin Cajun seasoned chicken cutlets in a hot pan. Once Upon a Chef and Jessica Gavin use a red wine vinegar and Dijon vinaigrette and cook the chicken in the bacon fat. This one follows Spend With Pennies' dressing and cutlets, seasons the chicken with paprika in place of Cajun spice, and cooks it in the bacon fat.
